narrative.northStar: Words at Rest Beside Still Waters
narrative.overview:
waitforit-theme is a personal-site theme for six kinds of content, not a product shell. Every page is a sheet of warm paper — a radial veil of `--wf-paper` — at rest beside a low meadow and a narrow stream: an original WebGL2 landscape with fixed ground, wind-shaped grass and softly blended stream ripples, fading out where the paper becomes solid. A static grain tile sits between veil and frame. A fixed frame holds the only chrome a page ever gets: the brand emblem, the word MENU, a footer. Nothing scrolls but content. A blog post or an essay is a mono date above a serif reading column; a project is a flat hairline card with no fill, radius, or shadow. The site should read like a printed page, not the outside of an app.

The austerity is structural, not stylistic. Two OFL typefaces: Newsreader for the human voice, Commit Mono for the machine voice. Thirteen color tokens: paper and ink by day, their night counterparts under `[data-theme="night"]`, and one moonlight that must survive both lights. Two radii in the whole system: `4px` on the language menu, `5px` on a keycap. No raised card, no chip, no filled button, no accent hue; the only card form is the flat project grid, which never lifts. Depth is never faked with elevation: the scene sits under the veil, the veil under the grain, the grain under the frame, and that stack is the entire trick.

Motion is a small fixed vocabulary: pages arrive in 520ms and leave in 220ms, content enters in 300ms, the menu opens in 240ms and closes in 180ms, the theme cross-fades in 900ms while scene, veil, and grain change light together, and the subscribe line confirms in 720ms. Everything respects `prefers-reduced-motion` — every duration token becomes 0ms and the landscape freezes on its first frame — and nothing ever moves to attract attention.
keyCharacteristics: Two typefaces only: Newsreader (OFL variable serif, true italic) for display, title, and reading; Commit Mono (OFL) for body, UI, form, label, and code.
Thirteen color tokens: `paper` and `ink` by day, `night-paper` and `night-ink` by night, plus a muted ink, a hairline, and a `moonlight` that survives both lights.

One brand emblem: the user-supplied silhouette. One interaction ornament: an original eight-ray four-point star, used as the cursor and a hover reward — never as static decoration and never as a bullet.
One fixed frame (75px, 40px at ≤800px, 28px at ≤520px) around one centered column of `min(100%, 760px)`.
Four stacked layers and no page background: scene, then veil, then grain, then frame.
Three shipped page types: blog and essays share one serif reading column under a mono date; projects are a flat hairline card grid linking out to a repository.
Quiet interaction instead of state chrome: dotted underlines turning solid, a 15px star revealed on hover, a 520ms page fade.

A declared font deviation: Newsreader and Commit Mono replace the reference's Plantin Now and Departure Mono, and the two `--wf-font-*` variables are the only override point for a site that self-hosts its own pair.

rules.name: The Paper Is Not a Background Rule
rules.body: There is no page background color. The surface is a fixed radial ellipse of paper (`--wf-veil-size: 72% 115%`, centered at `50% 48%`, alpha 0.985 at the center falling to 0 at the 96 percent stop), painted over the live scene. Do not replace it with a solid fill: a solid `#faf9f6` body would hide the landscape and turn the design back into a white page.

rules.name: The Two Faces Rule
rules.body: Newsreader and Commit Mono are the only typefaces this theme may use; every other family in a stack is a glyph fallback, not a design decision. A new role is assigned to one of the two voices and never to a third family. The Resting Lamb landscape is an intentional change of scene meaning; typography remains Newsreader and Commit Mono, and a site choosing its own pair overrides `--wf-font-serif` and `--wf-font-mono` with its own self-hosted OFL pair; the font files themselves never enter this repository or its build output.

rules.name: The Fixed Frame Rule
rules.body: The frame is chrome, not a container: it stays 75px, 40px, or 28px at the three breakpoints and content never paints over it. Nothing goes in the frame except the brand emblem, MENU, and the footer marks — no breadcrumbs, no progress bars, no floating buttons.

rules.name: The Stack Is the Depth Rule
rules.body: Depth comes from layer order, never from elevation on content: the scene under the veil, the veil under the grain, the grain under the frame. Content never floats, and no shadow may be added to a reading surface; the three functional shadows above are the whole vocabulary.

rules.name: The Rounded Corner Is a Signal Rule
rules.body: `4px` means this surface floats over the scene; `5px` means this is a key. No other value is allowed, and a rounded button, input, card, or code block is a defect rather than a variation. The star keeps its geometry in every use and is never recolored, cached, or restyled.

rules.name: The Bare Chrome Rule
rules.body: Every action is text: no fill, no border, no raised card, no chip, and no icon set. If an element cannot be expressed as a word, a dot underline, a hairline, or the star, or the brand emblem, it does not belong in this theme. Component snippets must stay paste-sized and self-contained, and any reference component that ships is a decision recorded with its reason in the snippet inventory.

dos: Keep the reading column at `min(100%, 760px)` and the serif at 18 to 20px; the reading column is the product.

Declare the font substitution in the repository: Newsreader and Commit Mono are the theme's only faces, and `--wf-font-serif` and `--wf-font-mono` are the only override point for a site that self-hosts its own OFL pair.
Reserve Commit Mono for chrome, meta, forms, and code, and set every human voice in Newsreader.
Express hierarchy with size, ink opacity between 60 and 80 percent, and hairlines, never with hue, weight, or fills.
Use the dotted underline — `0.06em` thick at `0.14em` offset, solid on hover — plus a 15px star as the single interaction language for links.
Let the scene, veil, and grain carry depth, and keep content surfaces flat and shadowless.
Honour the duration tokens and `prefers-reduced-motion`: at reduce, every motion token is 0ms and the landscape freezes on its first frame.
Ship a skip link and keep every chrome control reachable by keyboard and pointer, even though the reference site does not.
donts: Don't introduce a third typeface, and never let Plantin Now, Plantin, or Departure Mono into the repository or its build output; the only permitted deviation is the `--wf-font-*` override with self-hosted OFL faces.
Don't introduce an accent hue, a raised card, a chip, a filled button, or a shadow beyond the three functional ones; flat hairline project cards are the only card form.
Don't fake weight or slant: no `text-shadow` thickening and no synthetic italic; mono stays at its 400 token weight and serif emphasis uses Newsreader's true italic.
Don't paint a solid page background or stack an opaque panel over the scene; the drawn landscape must stay visible outside the veil.
Don't animate anything to draw attention — no pulses, no autoplay, no scroll-jacking; the only continuous motion is the grass tips and stream textures.
Don't use the interaction star asset as static ornament; lists use the star glyph and the asset belongs to pointer and chrome. Procedural, stationary sky points belong only to the scene.
Don't hardcode a token value in a template or a stylesheet; add the token first and consume it as `var(--wf-*)`, so a theme-wide change stays a one-file change.
Don't copy the reference's known defects as patterns: the missing skip link, the English flash before client-side i18n, and the light-mode nav overlap are documented gaps, not design decisions.
